hero.headline: Supreme Court rules against AT&T and Verizon in location data case
hero.body:
The Supreme Court upheld the Federal Communications Commission's authority to impose fines on wireless carriers, rejecting AT&T and Verizon's challenge to the agency's enforcement process. The 8-1 decision handed a significant victory to the Trump administration and affirmed the FCC's power to penalize companies without requiring a jury trial.

The case centered on whether the FCC's in-house proceedings for imposing penalties violated the carriers' constitutional right to a jury trial. AT&T and Verizon had challenged the agency's system for levying fines, arguing that the administrative process deprived them of due process protections guaranteed by the Constitution. The court disagreed with their position.

The fines in question stemmed from the carriers' practice of selling customer location data. The FCC had determined that AT&T and Verizon violated regulations governing how wireless companies handle sensitive information about their customers. Location data can reveal detailed patterns about where people travel and spend time, raising significant privacy concerns among consumer advocates and lawmakers.

The Supreme Court's decision preserves the FCC's ability to enforce its regulations through administrative penalties without the added requirement of jury trials. This ruling has broader implications for how federal agencies can regulate telecommunications companies and enforce compliance with data protection rules. The decision allows the FCC to maintain an efficient enforcement process without the delays and complications that jury trials might introduce.

For AT&T and Verizon, the ruling means the penalties imposed by the FCC will stand. The carriers will be required to pay the fines the agency levied for selling location data without proper customer consent or disclosure.

The case represents an important test of federal regulatory authority over the telecommunications industry. Wireless carriers handle vast amounts of personal information about their customers, including real-time location data that reveals sensitive details about daily movements and activities. The sale of this data to third parties has drawn criticism from privacy advocates who argue it poses risks to consumers.

Only one justice dissented from the majority opinion in the 8-1 ruling. The court's overwhelming support for the FCC's position demonstrates broad judicial agreement that regulatory agencies need the flexibility to enforce penalties without requiring jury proceedings.

This decision may have consequences beyond the specific case involving AT&T and Verizon. It establishes precedent for how other federal agencies can challenge companies and enforce regulations in their respective industries. The ruling suggests the Supreme Court is comfortable with administrative enforcement mechanisms when agencies have clear authority to regulate specific conduct.

The case also reflects ongoing tensions around how telecommunications companies collect, use, and sell customer data. As wireless carriers continue to hold unprecedented amounts of personal information about millions of Americans, the FCC and other regulators face pressure to strengthen protections and hold companies accountable when they misuse that data.

cards.headline: House approves Ukraine aid in defiance of Trump and Republican leadership
cards.teaser: The chamber passed legislation providing assistance to Ukraine and imposing sanctions on Russia, breaking with the president's foreign policy stance.
cards.body:
The House passed legislation Thursday to aid Ukraine and impose sanctions on key segments of Russia's economy, voting 226-195 despite objections from Republican leaders. The bill represents the chamber's second major foreign policy break with Trump this week, following a war powers resolution the day before aimed at halting U.S. military action against Iran.

Republican leaders warned the bill would undermine ongoing negotiations they believe could achieve stronger results. The vote reflects growing impatience among House members with Trump's approach to the war in Ukraine.

cards.headline: Senate advances $70 billion immigration enforcement budget as vulnerable Republicans break ranks
cards.body:
The Senate moved toward passing a $70 billion budget reconciliation package to fund immigration enforcement agencies after a marathon of amendment votes. Vulnerable Republicans broke with their party on several amendments during the voting session.

Senate Republicans defeated a Democratic amendment 49-50 sponsored by Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer. The amendment would have prohibited the Department of Justice from establishing a $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund. The vote saw at least one Republican defection as the measure failed by a single vote.

Sen. Susan Collins of Maine cast her 10,000th consecutive Senate vote during the session. Collins voted in favor of a Democratic motion to send the reconciliation package back to the Judiciary Committee. She stood at her desk wearing a red dress and blue blazer with brass buttons when the clerk called her name.

The reconciliation process allows the Senate to pass budget legislation with a simple majority, bypassing the usual 60-vote threshold required to overcome a filibuster. The $70 billion package represents a significant investment in immigration enforcement infrastructure and personnel at federal agencies responsible for border security and immigration law enforcement.

The voting session featured numerous amendments as lawmakers sought to shape the final legislation. The measure now moves closer to final passage as the Senate continues processing remaining amendments and preparing for a vote on the underlying bill.

cards.headline: Trump directs $800 million to struggling coal industry using emergency powers
cards.teaser: The administration announced hundreds of millions of dollars in support for coal production, including funding for a new export terminal and plant modernization.
cards.body:
President Trump announced an $800 million plan to support the coal industry, using emergency powers to direct the funds. The package includes $700 million for coal investment, $19 million to modernize a Wisconsin coal plant, and funding for a new coal export terminal in Oakland.

Trump characterized coal as beautiful and clean during the announcement. Reuters reported the administration is using emergency authority to channel the money to the industry, which has faced financial challenges in recent years. The plan represents a significant federal intervention to prop up coal production and infrastructure.

cards.headline: China's Xi Jinping Visits North Korea Amid Shifting Alliance Dynamics
cards.teaser: The Chinese president travels to Pyongyang to meet with a North Korean leader whose growing partnership with Russia has reduced his reliance on Beijing.
cards.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping is visiting Pyongyang for talks with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. The trip comes as North Korea has strengthened its alliance with Russia, altering the traditional dynamic in which China served as the isolated nation's primary patron and diplomatic lifeline.

Xi faces a more emboldened North Korean dictator whose reduced dependence on China has shifted the regional balance. The enhanced Russia-North Korea partnership has provided Kim with additional strategic options and economic support, potentially diminishing Beijing's leverage over its neighbor.

cards.headline: Hezbollah Rejects Ceasefire Agreement Between Israel and Lebanon
cards.teaser: Hezbollah has rejected a ceasefire agreement reached between Israel and the Lebanese government, with the group's leader declaring the U.S.-brokered deal amount.
cards.body:
The United States announced a ceasefire agreement between Israel and Lebanon on Wednesday night following fresh negotiations. However, Hezbollah, the Iran-backed militant group that operates independently in southern Lebanon, rejected the deal. Hezbollah's leader characterized the agreement as surrender, objecting to terms negotiated without the group's participation.

The rejection raises questions about the ceasefire's viability. Israeli strikes killed eight people in Lebanon following the announcement, and fighting continued between Israeli forces and Hezbollah. Israel has stated it will continue its ground operation in southern Lebanon despite the agreement with the Lebanese government. A U.N. peacekeeper was also killed and others wounded by mortar fire in southeastern Lebanon.

cards.headline: Zelensky Calls for Direct Talks With Putin in Open Letter
cards.teaser: Ukraine's president has proposed face-to-face negotiations with Russia's leader, saying only direct engagement can end the war.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has published an open letter directly to Russian President Vladimir Putin calling for face-to-face negotiations. The letter, Zelenskyy's first public direct address to Putin since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022, emphasizes that only direct engagement between the two countries can end the war.

In the letter, Zelenskyy proposes holding talks in a neutral third country. The appeal comes as international attention shifts, with U.S. focus turning toward other regional priorities including Iran.

cards.headline: Protests Escalate in Albania Over Kushner-Backed Luxury Resort Project
cards.teaser: Days of demonstrations have erupted over a planned resort development linked to Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump on Albania's pristine coastline.
cards.body:
Demonstrations have erupted in Albania over a luxury resort development on Sazan Island backed by Jared Kushner. Environmental campaigners and opponents argue the project would damage a protected coastal environment, while the Albanian government says it will help transform the nation's economy.

The resort plan, linked to the Trump family, has drawn criticism from environmental groups and resistance from the public. European Union officials have also expressed concerns about the large-scale tourism development in one of Albania's undeveloped coastal regions.

cards.headline: Missing Sherpa Guide Found Alive on Mount Everest After Week-Long Ordeal
cards.teaser: A Sherpa who disappeared on Everest was discovered crawling toward base camp after surviving six days alone without food or oxygen as his family had begun funeral rites.
cards.body:
Hillary Dawa Sherpa has been rescued after going missing on Mount Everest. A cleaning crew spotted him crawling toward Base Camp six days after he disappeared at higher altitude. His family had already begun funeral rites before learning of his survival.

Climber Chris Thrall recounted losing contact with Dawa Sherpa during their expedition. The guide's ability to descend the mountain alone and survive such an extended ordeal in extreme high-altitude conditions is considered remarkable.

cards.headline: Ireland Increases Military Spending Amid European Security Concerns
cards.teaser: The Irish government is working to address gaps in its armed forces as worries grow across Europe about threats from Russia.
cards.body:
Ireland is moving to strengthen its military capabilities as concern rises across Europe over potential threats from Russia. The Irish government has acknowledged it is working to address significant gaps in its defense forces, which reflect the country's long tradition of neutrality.

European nations have increasingly viewed military preparedness as urgent following Russia's actions in recent years. Ireland has been identified as a weak link in European defense, prompting the government to commit to bulking up its armed forces. The shift represents a notable change for a nation that has historically maintained a neutral stance in international conflicts.

cards.headline: Zelensky Calls for Direct Talks With Putin in Open Letter
cards.teaser: Ukraine's president has proposed face-to-face negotiations with Russia's leader, saying only direct engagement can end the war.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has published an open letter directly to Russian President Vladimir Putin calling for face-to-face negotiations. The letter, Zelenskyy's first public direct address to Putin since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022, emphasizes that only direct engagement between the two countries can end the war.

In the letter, Zelenskyy proposes holding talks in a neutral third country. The appeal comes as international attention shifts, with U.S. focus turning toward other regional priorities including Iran.

cards.headline: US Deploys Flies and Dogs to Combat Screwworm Outbreak
cards.teaser: America faces its first screwworm outbreak since 1966, with the flesh-eating insect spreading concern across the southern United States.
cards.body:
The United States is deploying specialized flies and trained detection dogs to combat a screwworm outbreak in the southern United States. This marks the first appearance of the flesh-eating insect in America since 1966, when it was previously eradicated from the country.

Officials are using sterile flies as part of their containment strategy to prevent the parasite from becoming established in American agricultural regions. The screwworm's return has triggered an urgent response to protect both livestock and potentially human health.

hero.headline: Murder charge dismissed against Arkansas sheriff candidate who killed daughter's alleged abuser
hero.body:
A judge has dismissed the murder charge against Aaron Spencer, an Arkansas sheriff candidate who fatally shot a man accused of sexually abusing his daughter, according to court documents.

Spencer had been charged with murder following the shooting. He was running for Lonoke County sheriff when the incident occurred. The specific legal reasoning behind the judge's decision to dismiss the case has not been disclosed publicly.

Spencer stated that he acted to protect his daughter from someone he believed had sexually abused her. Despite facing the criminal charge, he continued his campaign for sheriff throughout the legal proceedings, bringing significant attention to the case.

The dismissal concludes the criminal case that had been pending against Spencer. Prosecutors had initially moved forward with murder charges despite Spencer's stated justification for his actions. The case raised broader questions about the boundaries between vigilante justice and a parent's legal right to protect their child.

The shooting sparked debate about when lethal force can be justified in defense of family members. Spencer characterized his actions as a protective response to abuse, while prosecutors initially determined that the circumstances warranted a murder charge. The judge's decision to dismiss the case represents a significant legal development for the sheriff candidate.

The case drew attention because it intersected criminal justice considerations, family protection claims, and local electoral politics. Spencer had remained on the ballot for the Lonoke County sheriff position throughout the proceedings. The dismissal of charges removes the major obstacle that had overshadowed his campaign.

The outcome allows Spencer to continue pursuing elected office without the burden of pending criminal charges. The case had generated considerable public interest, with many people following the legal proceedings as they unfolded alongside his campaign activities.

The specific grounds for dismissal have not been explained in available court documents, leaving questions about whether the judge found insufficient evidence, legal defects in the charges, or other factors that led to the decision to dismiss.

This case reflected broader tensions in the legal system regarding how far individuals can go in defending family members against harm. While laws generally protect parents who take reasonable steps to protect their children, the shooting raised questions about whether lethal force fell within legally acceptable bounds.

The dismissal concludes what had been a closely watched legal matter in Arkansas. Spencer can now focus exclusively on his campaign for Lonoke County sheriff, a position that carries significant authority over law enforcement in the county. The resolution of the criminal case removes a major complication from his path to elected office.

cards.headline: Trump directs $800 million to struggling coal industry using emergency powers
cards.teaser: The administration announced hundreds of millions of dollars in support for coal production, including funding for a new export terminal and plant modernization.
cards.body:
President Trump announced an $800 million plan to support the coal industry, using emergency powers to direct the funds. The package includes $700 million for coal investment, $19 million to modernize a Wisconsin coal plant, and funding for a new coal export terminal in Oakland.

Trump characterized coal as beautiful and clean during the announcement. Reuters reported the administration is using emergency authority to channel the money to the industry, which has faced financial challenges in recent years. The plan represents a significant federal intervention to prop up coal production and infrastructure.

cards.headline: John Bolton to plead guilty in classified documents case
cards.teaser: The former Trump national security adviser reached a plea agreement over his mishandling of sensitive national security information.
cards.body:
John Bolton, former national security adviser under President Trump, has reached a plea deal in his classified documents case. According to sources, Bolton agreed to plead guilty to one count of illegal retention of sensitive national security information. The agreement is subject to court approval.

The Justice Department filed charges against Bolton in 2025. Bolton left Trump's first administration and later became a prominent critic of the president.

cards.headline: California ballot counting continues as slow results draw criticism
cards.teaser: The state's lengthy vote tabulation process has made it a target for critics, but officials say the pace does not indicate problems with election integrity.
cards.body:
California's ballot counting process is taking weeks or potentially a month to complete, drawing criticism from those questioning the delays. The extended timeline applies to statewide races and Los Angeles elections, where large volumes of mail ballots require additional time for processing and verification.

State law permits ballots postmarked by election day to be counted if they arrive within days of the vote, which contributes to the lengthy tabulation period. Election officials and news organizations including the AP and BBC have noted that slow results in California are an expected consequence of the state's mail-in voting system rather than indicators of election integrity problems.

cards.headline: Spencer Pratt and Nithya Raman compete for second place in Los Angeles mayoral race
cards.teaser: The reality television personality and city council member are in a tight contest for a runoff spot as new ballot counts continue.
cards.body:
Nithya Raman, a Los Angeles city council member, has narrowed the gap with Spencer Pratt in the race for second place in the mayoral primary. The latest ballot count updates show the two candidates competing to advance to a runoff election.

Pratt, known for his reality television career, surged in the race as voters expressed dissatisfaction with incumbent Mayor Karen Bass. Fox News reported that angry voters sent a message to Bass by supporting alternative candidates. NBC News is tracking live results as additional ballots are processed in the closely watched contest.

cards.headline: Former congressman George Santos threatens NPR reporter over investigation story
cards.teaser: Santos made a violent threat against a journalist who reported on new federal investigations into his activity on a prediction market site.
cards.body:
Rewritten Card:

Federal authorities are investigating whether George Santos engaged in insider trading through bets placed on Kalshi, a prediction market platform. According to NPR's reporting, the former congressman allegedly wagered on whether he would attend Trump's State of the Union address in February.

After NPR published this investigation, Santos made a violent threat against the reporter who broke the story. Santos later denied making the threat, but NPR documented both the threat and his false denials.

cards.headline: Senate Republicans defeat Democratic attempt to block Trump's $1.8 billion fund
cards.teaser: The chamber voted down multiple efforts to eliminate a controversial fund during a vote session on broader spending legislation.
cards.body:
Senate Republicans narrowly blocked a Democratic effort to prevent President Trump from establishing a $1.8 billion fund to pay his allies. Democratic Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer proposed language to bar the payouts as part of Republican-backed legislation funding Trump's mass deportation campaign. The amendment failed along party lines.

Signs of dissent emerged within Trump's own party over the fund's purpose. Three GOP senators joined Democrats in opposing the measure, suggesting growing concern about the proposal among some Republicans. The vote occurred during a vote-a-rama procedure allowing unlimited amendments on budget legislation.

hero.headline: Wall Street banks prepare for SpaceX IPO, largest public offering ever
hero.body:
Elon Musk's SpaceX is preparing for what could become the largest initial public offering in history, with four major Wall Street banks competing for leading roles in the offering.

According to reports, SpaceX is considering Bank of America, JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, and Morgan Stanley to lead the public listing. The company is targeting a potential raise of up to $75 billion, which would value SpaceX at approximately $1.77 trillion if the offering proceeds as planned. The IPO is expected to launch in June next year.

The scale of the offering underscores the exceptional value and strategic importance the financial industry is placing on SpaceX. The company has evolved from a startup focused on reusable rocket technology into a diversified aerospace company with multiple revenue streams. SpaceX generates income from deploying reusable rockets for satellite launches and resupply missions to the International Space Station, operates the Starlink broadband service, and holds contracts with NASA worth approximately $1.1 billion annually.

According to recent reports, SpaceX's annual revenue is projected at $15.5 billion. The company was valued at $400 billion earlier and more recently in private share sales at $800 billion, reflecting significant growth in investor interest and market perception of its business prospects.

The successful execution of this IPO could reshape the landscape for large technology company offerings. Investors have become more discerning about profitability and sustainable business models in recent years, particularly after mixed market receptions for other major tech listings. SpaceX must convince public market investors that its business model spanning commercial launches, government contracts, and the Starlink service can deliver long-term returns.

The SpaceX offering arrives amid broader expectations for a significant year of technology IPOs. Other highly valued private companies including OpenAI and Anthropic are also the subject of IPO speculation, with reported valuations exceeding $100 billion. Industry analysts refer to such companies as "hectocorns."

Neil Wilson, an analyst at Saxo Capital Markets, noted that while Musk's Mars colonization ambitions generate headlines, investors will focus more closely on practical growth plans. These include orbital solar farms and datacenters. Wilson also suggested that major tech IPOs planned for the coming year will serve as a critical test for the sector, determining whether sky-high valuations reflect genuine business fundamentals or unsustainable speculation.

The involvement of multiple top-tier investment banks in the SpaceX offering reflects the extraordinary fees at stake. Underwriters will handle investor marketing, price setting, and the mechanics of the public debut, earning compensation based on the offering size.

Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase declined to comment on the reports. Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, and SpaceX did not respond to requests for comment.

cards.headline: Trump directs $700 million into coal using wartime powers
cards.teaser: The president is using emergency authorities to fund coal investments as energy costs rise during the Iran conflict.
cards.body:
President Trump announced a $700 million investment in the coal industry, invoking wartime economic authorities. The administration is responding to rising energy costs stemming from the conflict with Iran.

The funding is being positioned as a national security measure to strengthen domestic energy production during the international crisis.

cards.headline: S&P declines to change index rules for SpaceX early entry
cards.teaser: The index provider will not alter its requirements to allow the rocket company into benchmark indexes before meeting standard eligibility criteria.
cards.body:
S&P has decided against modifying its index inclusion rules to expedite SpaceX's entry into its benchmark indexes. The company will need to satisfy existing eligibility criteria before joining indexes like the S&P 500, the same requirements that apply to all large upcoming public offerings.

Index inclusion typically requires companies to meet specific thresholds for market capitalization, liquidity, and trading history as a public company. The decision affects how quickly SpaceX's shares could be added to major indexes that track trillions of dollars in passive investments.

cards.headline: Dow gains over 500 points as chip stocks decline following Broadcom earnings
cards.teaser: The blue-chip index reached a record closing high while the Nasdaq fell after the semiconductor company's results disappointed investors.
cards.body:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average surged more than 500 points to reach a record closing high, while the Nasdaq fell following Broadcom's disappointing earnings report. The divergence highlighted a rotation out of technology stocks that had driven recent market gains.

Broadcom's weak results sparked a selloff in semiconductor stocks, pressuring the Nasdaq and spreading weakness to Asian tech shares overnight. The S&P 500 rose alongside the Dow, buoyed by strength in industrial and financial sectors.

cards.headline: British Heart Foundation to close 150 charity shops
cards.teaser: The health charity cited an exceptionally challenging trading environment for the decision to shutter locations.
cards.body:
The British Heart Foundation plans to close 150 of its charity shops as it faces what the organization described as an exceptionally challenging trading environment. The closures will reduce the charity's retail footprint as it adapts to changing consumer habits and economic conditions.

Charity retail shops have faced pressure from rising operating costs, including rent and staffing expenses, alongside competition from online resale platforms. The British Heart Foundation operates shops that sell donated goods to fund cardiovascular research and health programs.

cards.headline: China regulates violence and misogyny in viral micro dramas
cards.teaser: Authorities are cracking down on content in the short-form video format that has surged in popularity.
cards.body:
Chinese regulators are taking action against violence and misogyny in micro dramas, a short-form video format that has become increasingly popular on social media platforms. The crackdown targets content that authorities view as sensationalist or harmful.

Micro dramas have grown rapidly as a form of entertainment, typically running just minutes per episode and designed for mobile viewing. The format has drawn criticism for often featuring extreme or provocative storylines. The regulatory intervention reflects broader government efforts to control online content and social media trends.

cards.headline: Hinge executive says young daters need AI assistance to make first moves
cards.teaser: The dating app's chief product officer cited loneliness and lack of confidence as challenges for users seeking relationships.
cards.body:
Jackie Jantos, a Hinge executive, says young adults in their twenties face significant barriers when initiating conversations on dating apps. He points to loneliness and lack of confidence as the main challenges preventing them from making first moves with potential matches.

The comments indicate that dating platforms are exploring AI-powered features to help users overcome these obstacles. Such tools would allow the apps to assist users in starting conversations, building on the algorithmic matching systems already widely used in the industry.

cards.headline: Anthropic revenue crosses $47 billion ahead of planned IPO
cards.teaser: The artificial intelligence company reported annualized revenue of $47 billion in May, up sharply from $9 billion at the end of last year.
cards.body:
Anthropic announced that its annualized revenue crossed $47 billion in May, a dramatic jump from roughly $9 billion at the end of 2025. The company is experiencing rapid growth as it prepares for an initial public offering.

President Daniela Amodei has dismissed skepticism about whether AI companies can generate sufficient financial returns to justify their valuations. The IPO will test how investors view Anthropic's business trajectory and the broader artificial intelligence sector's profitability potential.

cards.headline: Airbnb CEO plans to launch artificial intelligence lab
cards.teaser: Brian Chesky said the company avoided earlier AI partnerships because existing products were not ready for deployment.
cards.body:
Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky announced plans to establish a new artificial intelligence laboratory. The move reflects the company's decision to develop AI capabilities in-house rather than partnering with existing providers. Chesky previously explained that Airbnb had not pursued large language model partnerships because available products did not meet the company's requirements.

The initiative signals that Chesky views AI as a key component of Airbnb's future product strategy and development.

cards.headline: Meta adds facial recognition code to AI app on millions of phones
cards.teaser: Code for an unreleased facial recognition feature was discovered in Meta's AI application, raising privacy concerns.
cards.body:
Wired reported finding code for facial recognition technology in Meta's AI app that has been distributed to millions of phones. The feature has not been publicly released or announced by the company. The discovery has prompted questions about Meta's plans for the technology and how it might be used in connection with the company's smart glasses products.

The presence of the code suggests Meta is developing facial recognition capabilities for its consumer AI products. Privacy advocates have raised concerns about the technology, particularly given Meta's history with user data. A lawsuit and leaked internal memo related to the feature have emerged, according to reports.

cards.headline: New app blocks ads across iPhone and Mac applications
cards.teaser: Filtr uses features in Apple's latest software to prevent ads from loading inside apps and web browsers.
cards.body:
A privacy tool called Filtr now blocks advertisements across iPhone and Mac applications. The app leverages new features in the latest Apple operating system to extend ad blocking beyond web browsers to other apps.

Filtr, which was previously available as a Safari ad blocker, works on iPhones, iPads, and Macs running the newest Apple software versions. This expanded capability allows users to prevent ads from loading in nearly all applications on their Apple devices.

cards.headline: Mangrove forests recover after decades of destruction
cards.teaser: Coastal mangrove ecosystems are growing back in areas where they were previously destroyed by human activity.
cards.body:
Mangrove forests around the world are making a remarkable recovery after suffering widespread destruction from human activity. These coastal wetland ecosystems are now regrowing in areas where they had previously disappeared, marking a significant environmental turnaround.

The resurgence brings substantial benefits to both nature and people. Mangrove forests shield coastal communities from storms and flooding while sequestering large quantities of carbon. They also provide essential habitat for wildlife and support fisheries that many coastal populations rely on for food and livelihoods.

cards.headline: Viral robot videos distort public understanding of capabilities
cards.teaser: Demonstrations of humanoid robots spreading online can mislead viewers about what the machines can actually do.
cards.body:
Robot demonstrations that go viral on the internet often create distorted perceptions of what robotic systems can accomplish. Videos of humanoid robots performing tasks can make the technology appear more advanced than it actually is. Experts caution that edited footage and controlled environments may not represent how robots perform in real-world conditions.

The gap between viral demonstrations and actual capabilities matters as companies seek investment and public support for robotics development. Misleading impressions can lead to unrealistic expectations about when robots will be able to perform complex tasks autonomously in everyday settings.

hero.headline: Browns trade Myles Garrett to Rams for Jared Verse and three draft picks
hero.body:
The Cleveland Browns have traded star edge rusher Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams in exchange for linebacker Jared Verse and three draft selections. The blockbuster deal reshapes both franchises and sends one of the league's most dominant defensive players to a Super Bowl contender.

Garrett, 30, is a two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year and seven-time Pro Bowl selection. Since the Browns selected him first overall in 2017, he has established himself as one of football's premier pass rushers. He holds the record for most sacks (125.5), pressures (413) and tackles for loss (149) among all players since his draft year. In 2025, Garrett set the single-season sacks record with 23.

The defensive end had requested a trade from Cleveland in 2024 after the Browns finished 3-14, expressing his desire to play for a championship contender. A month later, he signed a four-year, $160 million extension that made him the highest-paid non-quarterback in league history at the time. The deal included $122.8 million in guaranteed money and averaged $40 million annually.

Despite Garrett's individual excellence, the Browns continued struggling. They finished 2025 with a 5-12 record and missed the playoffs for the second consecutive year, though Garrett earned All-Pro recognition. Head coach Kevin Stefanski was fired and replaced by Todd Monken, the former Baltimore Ravens offensive coordinator. Monken stated he had not met face-to-face with Garrett since being hired.

General manager Andrew Berry facilitated the trade after he and Garrett agreed to modify the contract in March, deferring option payments across the 2026-28 seasons. This restructuring allowed the organization to proceed with the deal.

"As discussions intensified we were stuck at a legitimate crossroads: do we hold on to a truly generational player who has become the identity of our team, or do we make the difficult decision that we think is best for the organization over the long run?" Berry said after announcing the trade.

The Browns received Verse, a 2027 first-round pick, a 2028 second-round selection and a 2029 third-round choice. Verse, 25, was a first-round pick by the Rams in 2024 and earned Defensive Rookie of the Year honors. He has recorded 12 career sacks and 22 tackles for loss while also earning Pro Bowl selection this past season.

For the Rams, the acquisition represents an aggressive bid to win immediately. Los Angeles, which lost to the Seattle Seahawks in last season's NFC championship game, has a history of making bold trades. The team won the Super Bowl in 2022 with Matthew Stafford after acquiring him from Detroit. Super Bowl LXI will be played at SoFi Stadium in February, where the Rams won their previous championship.

cards.headline: Yankees place Aaron Judge on injured list with stress fracture in rib
cards.teaser: The Yankees will be without their MVP slugger for significant time after imaging revealed a stress fracture in Judge's right side.
cards.body:
Aaron Judge has been placed on the injured list after medical imaging revealed a stress fracture in a rib on his right side. The injury is expected to keep the Yankees outfielder and reigning MVP out of action for a substantial period as the team awaits further clarity on a recovery timeline.

Jazz Chisholm Jr. provided an update on Judge's condition as the Yankees assess their offensive depth during the absence. The team faces questions about whether their lineup has enough production to remain competitive without their most dangerous hitter in the middle of the order.

cards.headline: Texas softball wins second straight national championship with win over Texas Tech
cards.teaser: The Longhorns defeated Texas Tech 4-1 in the Women's College World Series Finals to claim back-to-back NCAA titles.
cards.body:
Texas defeated Texas Tech 4-1 to win the 2026 Women's College World Series championship, capturing its second consecutive national title. The Longhorns prevailed in an all-Texas Finals matchup that concluded the tournament in Oklahoma City.

The victory gives Texas back-to-back championships and extends the program's dominance in college softball. Texas Tech head coach Gerry Glasco discussed his pitching decisions after the first game of the Finals series, but the Red Raiders were unable to overcome the Longhorns' offensive and defensive execution.

cards.headline: Red Sox send struggling Brayan Bello to Triple-A Worcester
cards.teaser: Boston optioned starting pitcher Brayan Bello to its top minor league affiliate after another poor performance against Baltimore.
cards.body:
The Boston Red Sox have optioned starting pitcher Brayan Bello to Triple-A Worcester following another difficult outing against the Orioles. The move comes as the Red Sox address ongoing struggles in their starting rotation.

Bello's latest start contributed to a pattern of ineffective performances by Boston starters. The organization decided Bello would benefit from time at the Triple-A level to work on his mechanics and regain the form that previously made him a key part of the rotation. The Red Sox will look to other options in their rotation while Bello works to return to the major league roster.

cards.headline: Kelsey Mitchell scores 25 as Fever beat Dream in Commissioner's Cup opener
cards.teaser: Indiana defeated Atlanta despite Caitlin Clark dealing with illness during the game, with Mitchell leading the scoring.
cards.body:
Kelsey Mitchell scored 25 points to lead the Indiana Fever past the Atlanta Dream in their Commissioner's Cup opener at Gainbridge Fieldhouse. The victory came despite Caitlin Clark vomiting at halftime after attempting to eat applesauce, though she returned to contribute to the win.

The matchup featured two of the WNBA's most prominent rookies, with Clark and Angel Reese both playing significant roles. Mitchell's performance provided the offensive firepower Indiana needed, while Clark overcame her halftime illness to help secure the victory in the special tournament competition.

cards.headline: Formula 1 extends Las Vegas Grand Prix contract through 2037
cards.teaser: The race will remain on the calendar for at least another decade after F1 and the Las Vegas Convention and Visitors Authority agreed to a 10-year extension.
cards.body:
Formula 1 has extended its Las Vegas Grand Prix contract for an additional 10 years, keeping the race on the calendar until at least 2037. The agreement was reached with the Las Vegas Convention and Visitors Authority.

The Las Vegas Grand Prix has become a prominent fixture on the F1 schedule since its recent debut, showcasing the sport's expanding footprint in the United States.

cards.headline: Shakira to perform at 2026 World Cup opening ceremony in Mexico
cards.teaser: The Colombian pop star will perform her official tournament song at the competition's opening ceremony.
cards.body:
Colombian pop star Shakira will perform at the 2026 World Cup opening ceremony in Mexico. She will perform the official song for the tournament during the opening festivities.

The 2026 World Cup will be co-hosted by the United States, Canada, and Mexico, with the opening ceremony held in Mexico.

hero.headline: Actor James Handy Killed in Tarzana Stabbing, Girlfriend's Son Arrested
hero.body:
James Handy, an 81-year-old character actor with a decades-long career in television and film, was fatally stabbed at his home in the Tarzana neighborhood of Los Angeles on Wednesday, June 3. The Los Angeles Police Department arrested his girlfriend's son in connection with the killing.

According to law enforcement, the suspect called 911 to confess to the crime. Police responded to Handy's residence and took the suspect into custody without incident. Authorities have not released the suspect's identity or disclosed a motive for the attack.

Handy was perhaps best known for his role as the bartender in the 2022 film Top Gun: Maverick. He also appeared in Jumanji and maintained a steady presence in Hollywood through numerous guest appearances on television shows throughout his career. His work spanned multiple generations of film and television, showcasing his versatility as a character actor across different genres and formats.

The stabbing occurred at the home Handy shared with his girlfriend. Detectives continue to investigate the circumstances surrounding the fatal encounter, gathering evidence and interviewing witnesses related to the case. The investigation remains active as authorities work to understand what led to the violence.

Handy's death has drawn attention from colleagues and fans across the entertainment industry, who have paid tribute to the veteran performer. His extensive resume demonstrated his commitment to his craft and his ability to contribute meaningfully to productions throughout his long career in entertainment.

cards.headline: SAG-AFTRA Members Ratify Four-Year Contract With AI Provisions
cards.teaser: The union approved a deal covering synthetic actors and merging two pension funds, with over 91% voting in favor.
cards.body:
SAG-AFTRA members voted overwhelmingly to ratify a four-year contract with major studios, with 91.4% approval among those who cast ballots. The agreement includes new provisions governing the use of synthetic actors and merges the union's two pension funds into a consolidated retirement benefits structure.

The contract establishes conditions under which producers can deploy certain AI technologies in film and television productions. The deal addresses working conditions and compensation for actors across the industry while modernizing the union's pension system.

cards.headline: Madonna Performs Surprise Times Square Concert for Pride Month
cards.teaser: The pop icon debuted a new track from Confessions II during an outdoor performance in Manhattan.
cards.body:
Madonna transformed Times Square into an outdoor dance venue with a surprise performance marking Pride Month. The singer debuted a new track titled Love Sensation from her upcoming Confessions II album. She performed choreography that included dancing on a speaker box and playing air guitar.

The impromptu concert drew crowds to the Manhattan landmark. Madonna's appearance came without advance publicity, creating a spontaneous celebration in one of New York's most trafficked areas. The performance highlighted her continued presence as a cultural force in pop music.

cards.headline: Lil Durk Faces Additional Racketeering Charge
cards.teaser: Prosecutors filed a new indictment against rapper Durk Banks, whose attorneys maintain his innocence.
cards.body:
Rapper Lil Durk, whose legal name is Durk Banks, received a new racketeering charge from prosecutors. His legal team dismissed the additional indictment, with one attorney characterizing it as putting lipstick on a pig. The lawyers issued a statement declaring their client innocent.

Durk Banks is innocent, no matter how many indictments they want to throw at him, his attorneys said. The new charge adds to existing legal proceedings against the artist. The racketeering allegation represents an escalation in the case against the Chicago-based performer.

cards.headline: Trump Cancels Freedom 250 Concerts, Plans Rally With Lee Greenwood
cards.teaser: The president replaced the National Mall concert series with a political rally after most booked artists withdrew.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump has officially canceled the Freedom 250 concert series that was scheduled for the National Mall in Washington, D.C. The event fell apart after nearly all of the booked artists withdrew from the program.

Trump announced a replacement event billed as "the Greatest Rally EVER," with himself as the main attraction. Country singer Lee Greenwood will perform at the new rally-format gathering, which will center on a presidential address rather than functioning as a multi-artist music festival.

cards.headline: Jennifer Lopez and Brett Goldstein Star in Office Romance
cards.teaser: The Netflix romantic comedy pairs the actress as an airline CEO with the actor as her company's new lawyer.
cards.body:
Jennifer Lopez stars as Jackie Cruz, an airline CEO, opposite Brett Goldstein's Daniel Blanchflower, a newly hired company lawyer, in the Netflix romantic comedy Office Romance. The film brings together the unconventional pairing for a workplace romance that unfolds when Cruz summons Blanchflower to her office.

Lopez returns to the romantic comedy genre with the film, which has drawn mixed reviews. The Guardian noted that while Lopez proves a reliably charming lead, critics found the script and co-star Goldstein's performance lacked sufficient charm. Despite receiving middling critical reception, Lopez's recent Netflix projects have attracted strong streaming viewership.

cards.headline: Nick Bilton Named 60 Minutes Chief, Vows Editorial Independence
cards.teaser: The new leader of the CBS newsmagazine program pledged to pursue stories without interference as the show rebuilds.
cards.body:
Nick Bilton took over as chief of 60 Minutes and pledged to pursue stories "without fear or favor." His appointment follows CBS's firing of veteran correspondent Scott Pelley, who accused network executives of instructing him to inject falsehoods and bias into his reporting. Pelley claimed in a public statement that the new management was silencing employees and compromising editorial standards.

Pelley attributed the show's decades-long success to its integrity and quality journalism. His firing created uncertainty about the program's direction as CBS News navigates leadership changes and questions about whether remaining correspondents will stay with the organization.

hero.headline: Senate advances $70 billion immigration enforcement budget as vulnerable Republicans break ranks
hero.body:
The Senate moved toward passing a $70 billion budget reconciliation package to fund immigration enforcement agencies after a marathon of amendment votes. Vulnerable Republicans broke with their party on several amendments during the voting session.

Senate Republicans defeated a Democratic amendment 49-50 sponsored by Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer. The amendment would have prohibited the Department of Justice from establishing a $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund. The vote saw at least one Republican defection as the measure failed by a single vote.

Sen. Susan Collins of Maine cast her 10,000th consecutive Senate vote during the session. Collins voted in favor of a Democratic motion to send the reconciliation package back to the Judiciary Committee. She stood at her desk wearing a red dress and blue blazer with brass buttons when the clerk called her name.

The reconciliation process allows the Senate to pass budget legislation with a simple majority, bypassing the usual 60-vote threshold required to overcome a filibuster. The $70 billion package represents a significant investment in immigration enforcement infrastructure and personnel at federal agencies responsible for border security and immigration law enforcement.

The voting session featured numerous amendments as lawmakers sought to shape the final legislation. The measure now moves closer to final passage as the Senate continues processing remaining amendments and preparing for a vote on the underlying bill.

cards.headline: House passes Ukraine aid bill as 18 Republicans defy Trump
cards.teaser: Eighteen House Republicans joined Democrats to pass legislation authorizing military aid to Ukraine and sanctions on Russia.
cards.body:
The House passed legislation Thursday to aid Ukraine and impose sanctions on key segments of the Russian economy, with 18 Republicans joining Democrats in a 226-195 vote. The measure represents a significant break with Trump, coming just a day after the House approved a war powers resolution to halt U.S. military action against Iran.

Republican leaders had opposed the bill, arguing it would undermine ongoing negotiations. The vote demonstrates growing impatience among some Republicans with Trump's approach to the war in Ukraine.

cards.headline: FCC reviews $3 billion school internet program over screen time concerns
cards.teaser: The Federal Communications Commission is reviewing a program that subsidizes internet access for schools and libraries.
cards.body:
The Federal Communications Commission is reviewing the E-Rate program, which distributes $3 billion annually to help schools and libraries access the internet. FCC Chair Brendan Carr announced the review will examine the program's impact, with findings to be released.

The review reflects growing concerns about excessive screen time among children and its effects on their health and wellbeing.

cards.headline: Former HHS Secretary Xavier Becerra advances in California governor race
cards.teaser: Former Health and Human Services Secretary Xavier Becerra advanced to the general election in California's gubernatorial contest.
cards.body:
Former Health and Human Services Secretary Xavier Becerra advanced to the general election in the race to become California's next governor, according to Decision Desk HQ projections. Becerra will be one of two candidates competing in November to replace the outgoing governor.

Trump-backed Fox News commentator Steve Hilton and billionaire Tom Steyer are currently competing for the second spot in the general election. California voters will decide the gubernatorial race in November.

cards.headline: Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic gubernatorial primary
cards.teaser: Former Biden administration official Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for New Mexico governor.
cards.body:
Former Biden administration official Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for governor of New Mexico. Haaland previously served as Secretary of the Interior in the Biden administration.

Haaland could make history as the first female Native American governor if she wins the general election. She will face the Republican nominee in November's gubernatorial contest.

cards.headline: Trump schedules Washington rally for 250th anniversary of American independence
cards.teaser: President Trump announced a rally in Washington to commemorate America's 250th birthday.
cards.body:
President Trump announced a rally in Washington to commemorate America's 250th birthday. The announcement came after several artists dropped out of previous plans to perform at the upcoming Great American State Fair on the National Mall.

Trump said the event would not feature singers with no talent but big fees. He told performers to stay home and indicated the rally would take a different direction from the previously planned state fair entertainment.

cards.headline: Maine Senate candidate Graham Platner denies allegations in New York Times report
cards.teaser: Maine Democratic Senate candidate Graham Platner denied parts of a New York Times report containing allegations from former girlfriends.
cards.body:
Maine Democratic Senate candidate Graham Platner has rejected allegations reported by the New York Times, characterizing them as "politically motivated." The article included claims from past girlfriends describing incidents of physical misconduct and offensive remarks, as well as accusations from a Republican operative regarding womanizing and troubling comments about rape.

Platner has insisted the allegations are false and indicated he plans to continue his progressive campaign for the US Senate. He stated he has not considered withdrawing from the Maine Senate primary race.
